messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: sustained per-model TPM surge detected for model_family=polaris9b in region=us-west-2. 95th p50 latency creeping, error-rate 5.8%. Auto-sculpt triggered at 2026-03-15T02:12Z. Suggested mitigation: reduce model ceiling and enable fallbacks.

Jamie (oncall): I'm grabbing this. Can someone confirm customer-facing errors? @Samir @Jean

Samir: seeing a spike in 502s from the runtime for polaris9b. Root cause looks like KV-cache pressure + token-queue growth. Throughput to that pod group jumped ~6x.

Jean: Customer reports — ACME and Beacon both seeing 429s and slow streaming. Tickets #CS-4431 and #CS-4432. Beacon says they see function-calling errors specifically.

Jamie (oncall): ok plan: 1) immediately lower per-model ceiling (global TPM/RPM) for polaris9b 2) enforce per-customer soft floor so premium customers keep a fallback 3) disable function-calling on polaris9b temporarily 4) route new traffic to caspian11b for non-low-latency requests.

Matt (infra): I'm on step 1 and 3. Applying quick edits now.

Matt (infra): ```
# lower global limits
redwood-quota set --model polaris9b --tpm 120 --rpm 30 --region us-west-2
# disable function calling on the model
redwood-config set --model polaris9b --feature=function_calling --value=false
```

Samir: running health checks after the change. Watching queue depth and pod mem. Also pushing a KV-cache eviction hint to runtime.

Liz (ops): I'll carve out premium lanes. Setting per-customer override for ACME and Beacon so they have a guaranteed floor during this mitigation.

Liz (ops): ```
# per-customer floor for premium accounts
redwood-quota override --customer acme --model polaris9b --tpm 25 --note "mitigation: premium floor"
redwood-quota override --customer beacon --model polaris9b --tpm 20 --note "mitigation: premium floor"
```

Jean: Confirmed ACME tickets see reduced 429s, but Beacon still intermittent. Function-calling errors stopped after disable for some sessions; other errors are 503 from internal queue overflow earlier.

Samir: after lowering ceiling, pod memory pressure dropped ~40%, queue drain working. Error-rate down to 1.2%. Good so far.

Jamie (oncall): Good. Next: traffic routing — start redirecting non-critical or heavyweight calls to caspian11b. Matt, can you apply route rule for low-priority endpoints?

Matt (infra): putting a canary route. ```
# route 30% of non-authenticated streaming to caspian11b
redwood-router add-rule --match "path:/v1/generate AND priority!=high" --model caspian11b --pct 30 --region us-west-2 --note "mitigation canary"
```

Matt (infra): rule in. Monitoring impacts.

Jamie (oncall): Samir/Jean, collect customer impact summary for pager and CS. I'll escalate if we need broader quota carveouts. Also leaving a note for oncall handoff in 2 hours.

Samir: metrics look steady. Tail latencies for polaris9b back to normal band. Will keep an eye for regressions.

Jean: CS update: ACME reports degraded latency but acceptable. Beacon asked for ETA on function-calling re-enable. We'll coordinate after stability window.

Liz (ops): created a short-lived incident tag and annotated all quota changes in the audit log. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

Matt (infra): rolling back the function-calling disable is gated on runtime health. Proposed threshold: error-rate < 1% for 15m and queue depth < 100. If met, we re-enable at 10% traffic then ramp.

Jamie (oncall): Agreed. If health stays good, Samir you and Matt can coordinate re-enable. If anything spikes again, we fallback to full model throttle and increase caspian route.

Samir: setting an automated watch: if pod mem > 80% or tpm > 150 for polaris9b we notify and auto-escalate.

Samir: ```
redwood-monitor rule create --name polaris-guard --expr "pod_memory_percent>80 OR tpm>150" --action notify:oncall --region us-west-2
```

Jean: prepping CS messaging: short note for affected customers explaining temporary feature disable and fallback. Draft: "We've applied a temporary adjustment to polaris9b to improve reliability; function-calling is paused and we redirected some traffic to caspian11b. You may see slight changes in latency/behavior; premium requests retained a floor." Will post after Jamie reviews.

Jamie (oncall): thanks. I'll review and send. Handoff: I'm on for another 1.5h then handing to Matt overnight. Matt — please watch the monitor and increase caspian routing if error-rate creeps above 2% again.

Matt (infra): ack. I'll keep slack notifications on and update every 30m.

Liz (ops): logging post-mortem entry stub: "Polaris9b surge 2026-03-15 — immediate mitigations: lowered global TPM/RPM, per-customer floors for premium, disabled function-calling, routed non-critical traffic to caspian11b. Action items: improve KV-cache eviction heuristics, add automatic circuit-breaker at runtime, and add customer-visible maintenance banner in Console."

Jamie (oncall): thanks team. Closing the active escalation channel in 2 hours if stable. Leave any follow-ups here. (reaction :thumbsup:)
